title: Qcqs derived direct image of finite dimension preserves coproducts
statement: Let Lambda be a commutative ring and f : X \to Y a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Assume finite cohomological dimension for Lambda-module sheaves in the sense of [def-kun-cd]. Then the ordinary unbounded derived direct image Rf_* [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] preserves coproducts indexed by every type in the coefficient-module universe. Preservation is for the canonical coproduct cocone, including the empty family.

proof.text: The source filtered-colimit theorem for higher direct image and finite additivity show that all classical R^q f_* preserve coproducts: write a sum as the filtered colimit of finite subsums. The source single-sheaf comparison identifies these classical functors with the bounded-below higher-direct-image functors used by that theorem.

The source isZero_rightDerived_of_isZero_homology transfers the given unbounded single-sheaf vanishing bound to the classical derived functors, using the natural number max(d,0). Represent each derived input by a K-injective complex with injective terms. Preservation by every classical positive derived functor makes each term of their coproduct f_*-acyclic.

Use the source FiniteCohomologicalDimension dimension-shifting proof, the singleton identity case of the pointwise exact-complex theorem, to show that unbounded acyclic-term complexes compute the standard right derived functor. The source preservesColimitsOfShape_rightDerivedFunctor_of_rightDerived transports the termwise coproduct cocone through its natural standard-unit comparisons. Degree zero supplies preservation by f_* itself. The localization coproduct theorem identifies the resulting legs with the canonical derived coprojections. This proves the attached source theorem, including the empty indexing type.
